s02.note: Locate at t=0.00: the fit matched the tracker to 0.4 mm. Grasp: a top-down pinch at t=1.56-2.32. At t=6.24 (k04) the rod is lifted in the fingers. It is held only at the fingertips (rod centre 6.8 mm deep in the TCP frame, which plan.md calls 'at the tips'), and it sticks out from the pads asymmetrically (+4.6 mm). Insert: the move to 20 cm and the 144 deg rotation chain ran. At t=10.76 (k05) the rod still hangs from the fingertips, close above the blue fixture and tilted. By t=11.40 (k06) it has slipped out of the fingertips. It is lying on the board next to the fixture, and the wrist view shows it outside the fingers. In k08 (t=12.80) and k12 (t=15.60) it lies flat beside the fixture. Gripper width is -0.0002 (fully closed, empty) at t=16.88. The remaining move_to_joints calls (one FAIL at t=18.88 with err 22 mm) moved an empty hand. At t=21.44 the policy reported 'rod not seen in hand'. The rod lies on the board at the end. The tracker estimate stayed frozen at the initial pose all episode and cannot be trusted.

locate.evidence: Fit ctr [0.580,0.059,0.013], length 49.1 mm, rms 0.14 mm, n=3577. It agrees with the tracker (0.4 mm) and with the rod seen lying on the board at t=0.

grasp.evidence: k04 t=6.24: the rod is up with the hand at about 8 cm and moves with it. The grip is shallow, at the fingertips (6.8 mm depth, 4.6 mm off-centre). That weak hold is why it slipped later.

insert.evidence: The rod dropped out of the fingertip grip during the large reorientation chain, between t=10.76 (k05, still hanging near the fixture) and t=11.40 (k06, lying on the board beside the fixture). Nothing touched it, so it was a grip slip and not a collision. Everything after that was done with an empty hand (width about 0). At the end the rod lies flat on the board beside the fixture. The FAIL verdict is correct.

s03.note: Locate at t=0: the rod lay next to the blue fixture and every grasp candidate collided with obstacles, so the policy pushed the rod about 3 cm sideways (t=2-9). Grasp attempt 0 (t=8.6-9.2) was not a pads grip and was rejected. Attempt 1 (t=14.7-15.3, 2.5 mm higher) closed at width 4.5 mm, about 9.6 mm off the rod centre and at the tips (8.4 mm depth). k08 t=20.40: the rod is lifted in the fingers. Insert: only psi=-15 had a reachable chain (cost 113, 2976 hand-obstacle hits); it rotated 168 deg. k12 t=28.28: the rod hangs roughly vertical from the fingertips well above the fixture. Alignment 0 measured a 13.8 deg tilt and an 11.5 mm xy error. After that, 12 move_to_joints calls failed (t=26.5-37.3, err about 57 mm) with wrench at most 3 N. k16 t=31.80 and k22 t=38.76: the arm swings through large self-occluding configurations in open space, with no contact. The rod stayed in the fingers above the fixture (final.png: the wrist view shows it between the fingers, near vertical, above the fixture). The episode timed out before any descent, and insert never recorded a verdict. The rod was never in the bore.

locate.evidence: Fit ctr [0.354,0.042,0.013], length 48.9 mm, rms 0.23 mm. It agrees with the tracker to 0.5 mm.

grasp.evidence: After a push and one rejected attempt, k08 t=20.40 shows the rod lifted in the fingers. The grip is far from what the plan specifies: 9.6 mm off the rod centre (plan allows 10 mm) and at the tips. It held through the 168 deg rotation, and the rod is still in hand in final.png. Grasp used about 20 s of the 40 s budget.

insert.evidence: The stage never finished. After the rotation the rod was 13.8 deg off vertical and 11.5 mm off the bore. Then 12 joint moves failed (err about 57 mm, low wrench): the arm stalled in open space (reach/IK), not in a collision. It timed out at 40 s with the rod still in the fingers above the fixture and never lowered into the bore (k12, k16, k22, final).

s04.note: Locate at t=0: the rod lay on open board. Grasp at t=1.6-2.5: fingertip grip (7 mm depth, +4.5 mm off-centre). k04 t=7.80: the rod is lifted in the hand. Insert: the 127 deg rotation reached the plan within 0.8 deg. Alignment converged by align 2-4 (tilt about 0.1 deg, xy error about 0.5 mm, rod bottom at 0.052). k15 t=23.72: the rod is vertical below the fingers, directly over the bore. During the descent (stdout) the rod was blocked at the fixture top/bore entry and slid up in the fingers by 2.8 mm and then 3.4 mm. The spiral search claimed 'entered, rod bottom ~0.038', which is level with the fixture top at 0.0376, so at most about 0-1 mm in. The two re-alignments still read rod bottom 0.0449 (about 7 mm above the fixture top). Then three steps reported 'rod slid up -70 mm, F=0', so the mask fit had lost the rod or produced garbage. The policy released anyway at 'rod bottom ~0.0307', a value derived from those garbage readings. Sheet frames t=29-37: the rod is vertical in the fingers, resting at the bore mouth, not sunk in. Final.png at t=40: the gripper is open and above, and the rod lies horizontally across the top of the blue fixture, sticking out sideways. It fell over after the release. Insert never recorded a verdict (timeout).

locate.evidence: Fit ctr [0.448,0.019,0.013], length 49.0 mm, rms 0.20 mm. It agrees with the tracker to 0.6 mm.

grasp.evidence: k04 t=7.80: the rod is lifted to about 8 cm in the fingers and moves with the hand. It was held at the fingertips (7 mm depth) and stayed in hand through the rotation and alignment (k15 t=23.72).

insert.evidence: Alignment over the bore was good (tilt 0.1 deg, xy 0.5 mm). But the rod did not go down the bore: its tip stopped on the fixture top/bore entry and the rod slid up 3.4 mm in the fingers. That is a collision with the fixture, not a reach problem. The camera fit then broke ('slid up -70 mm'), and the policy released based on that bogus depth. It released with the rod at most about 1 mm into the bore, not 7 mm. In final.png (t=40) the rod has toppled and lies horizontally across the top of the fixture. The stage timed out with no verdict.
